This right here! I haven't finished watching Korra yet, but I've heard it got a bit of hate for being less amazing than ATLA. Is that really the case? I really enjoyed Season 1 (except for the love rectangle episode), and thought Asami was an especially fantastic character.

It's aimed towards ATLA's original audience, who are now their late teens and twenties, meaning the show is more mature and, at times, darker. (you probably know this from end of Book 1…) It's not a group of kids saving the world, it's a group of young adults trying to make sense of their lives while being thrown into the crossfires by bad guys and teaming up with wiser (and not-so-wise) adults. The series is more like an altered version of Zuko in Book 2 and 3 of ATLA rather than peppy, bright-eyed Aang from Book 1.

So it's the same world but it's not the same. (Though there is still plenty of waterbender recap-lesson-of-the-day monologues :P) I think that's where a lot of the hate comes from. I love it, but that's because I absolutely love ATLA and Bryke can do no wrong in my eyes. I also stopped participating in any online fan circles after Book 1 so I don't really know what specifically was criticized.
